findings.description: Critical: The plan creates global version registries, middleware, and a partial reorganized router tree without naming a v2 contract or a consumer that needs an overlap window; it covers only three route modules while the application now mounts 45 routers.
findings.resolution: Defer implementation, archive the speculative plan without syncing its delta spec, and require a named incompatible contract plus an independently migrating consumer before creating a second URL version.

findings.description: Critical: The catch-all sunset handler and global response middleware do not specify preservation of authentication, authorization, audit logging, CORS ordering, cache behavior, or the endpoint-specific legacy error boundaries.
findings.resolution: Do not add global sunset behavior speculatively. Any future version proposal must preserve the existing middleware security invariants and test both authenticated and unauthenticated behavior across the overlap.

findings.description: Nit: The plan conflates a URL major, the OpenAPI document version, and internal schema or protocol versions, even though the current workflow contract deliberately serves OpenAPI 2.0.0 under /api/v1.
findings.resolution: Document the version identities separately and reserve a URL-major change for an independently migrating HTTP compatibility boundary.

findings.description: The existing /api/v1 namespace, generated workflow clients, release-smoke gate, retired-route baseline, and CLI gen-eval suite provide a sound foundation for deferring a second live version until evidence changes.
findings.resolution: Retain these executable controls and cite them in the durable decision record.

findings.description: Critical: The first decision draft incorrectly treated all supported clients as coordinated, but manually installed iOS Shortcuts and the external agentic-assistant consumer have independent migration state.
findings.resolution: Inventory both consumers, assume they are non-lockstep until migration evidence proves otherwise, and make affected consumer deployment state part of the future v2 trigger.

findings.description: Critical: Optional response fields are not automatically backward-compatible because canonical Python response models forbid unknown properties and older clients can reject widened responses.
findings.resolution: Require executable oldest-client acceptance or a verified coordinated migration for every affected response change; do not classify response widening as additive by default.
